chart.title: Infant mortality rate
chart.subtitle: Estimated share of newborns who die before their first birthday. A rate of 1% means one death for every 100 live births.
chart.citation: United Nations Inter-agency Group for Child Mortality Estimation (2025)

Infant mortality rate of babies aged und.descriptionShort: Estimated number of deaths of children aged under one year, per 100 live births .
Infant mortality rate of babies aged und.descriptionKey: In countries hit by a humanitarian crisis, the UN IGME fits its trend with the crisis years set aside and then adds the crisis deaths back, so a few countries show a sharp one-year spike: Rwanda in 1994, Somalia in 2011, the Central African Republic in 2009, 2019 and 2022. For the Central African Republic these come from mortality surveys compiled by [Gang et al. (2023)](https://doi.org/10.1186/s13031-023-00514-z). They are all-cause excess deaths, added for the years each survey was run rather than spread across the longer period the surveys point to.
Infant mortality rate of babies aged und.descriptionProcessing:
Aggregate measures for continents are calculated by Our World in Data, using our definition of the continents found [here](https://ourworldindata.org/world-region-map-definitions#our-world-in-data).

We do this by calculating a weighted average from the national rates, using the respective denominators (e.g. live births or children under 5) as weights.
